## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvaraparivattana Sikkhāpada* ("Taking back a traded robe"), designated as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3, belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga. The rule provides that a Buddhist nun who reclaims or takes back a robe that she had previously given in exchange to another nun must relinquish the robe and confess the infraction (*nissaggiya pācittiya*). Modern English translations include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels exist in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np3*) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Parallels across other early Buddhist Vinaya lineages are preserved in the Chinese Canon, including the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 28), the Mahīśāsaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 21), and the Sarvāstivāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 22).
